rows.author: H081;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE UNIFORM IMPLEMENTATION OF NATIONAL SALARY SCHEDULE FOR THE PUBLIC SECTOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF SALARY STANDARDIZATION LAW AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Intends to address the decades-long problem that Philippine workers in poorer provinces 
and municipalities are paid less than their national counterparts which seems to stem from 
legislations such as R.A.No.6727 or the Wage Rationalization Act (1989); or R.A.No.6758 
or the Compensation and Position Classification Act of 1989; or R.A.No.7160 or the Local
Government Code, Book I Title III Sec. 81 and Book 2 Title V Chapter III Art.1 Sec.325.    

Aims to rectify the injustice by restoring the uniform implementation of the national salary 
schedule (under the Salary Standardization Law) for public sector employees throughout the 
country by repealing Sec.10 of E.O.No.201 s.2016 and by amending Sec.81 of R.A.No.7160.

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING SUBSTITUTE CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY TO REGULAR EMPLOYEES WHO RENDERED AT LEAST SIX CONTINUOUS MONTHS OF MERITORIOUS GOVERNMENT SERVICE
rows.abstract:
Proposes to extend the granting of substitute eligibility for long-time regular government employees who were able to render at least six (6) months of continuous meritorious service and/or at least with a satisfactory rating in the government including the national government agencies, LGUs, SUCs and GOCCs and all other government instrumentalities.

Refers \"substitute civil service eligibility\" to the qualification deemed to have been acquired by an individual through daily performance of his or her work to be recognized by the agency or instrumentality which utilized his or her services for the said period, for entrance into and promotion to the civil service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2019-02-04

rows.author: I083;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING FREE PUBLIC TERTIARY EDUCATION THROUGH INTRODUCTION OF COST OF ATTENDANCE AS PRIMARY DETERMINANT OF STATE-RUN UNIVERSITY OR COLLEGE'S ANNUAL FUNDING FROM THE GOVERNMENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10931, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"UNIVERSAL ACCESS TO QUALITY TERTIARY EDUCATION\"
rows.abstract:
Refers \"cost of attendance\" to the total amount a particular state-run university or college needs to provide education for a student per year, including the proportional cost per student for personnel services, maintenance and other operating expenses, and capital outlay.

Seeks to finance the actual \"cost of attendance\" of students, which shall also serve as guide for the Executive Department in preparing the national expenditure program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2019-02-04

rows.author: I083;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF THE FREE PUBLIC TERTIARY EDUCATION THROUGH NO COLLECTION OF ALL OTHER SCHOOL FEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10931, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"UNIVERSAL ACCESS TO QUALITY TERTIARY EDUCATION\"
rows.abstract:
Proposes to address the issue that several SUCs are circumventing R.A.NO.10931 through being 
able to establish and collect other school fees due to vague provision on the law.

Amends Sec.3(h) of R.A.No.10931 to read as follows: \"(h) Other school fees refers to fees charges by HEIs and technical-vocational institutions which cover other necessary costs supportive of instructions, specifically the following:  library fees, computer fees, laboratory fees, school ID fees, athletic fees, admission fees, development fees, guidance fees, handbook fees, entrance fees, registration fees, medical and dental fees, cultural fees and [other similar or related fees] ALL OTHER SCHOOL FEES.\"

rows.author: I083;

rows.author: I083;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND EXPANDING THE FREE PUBLIC TERTIARY EDUCATION THROUGH FORMULATION OF NATIONALIST, SCIENTIFIC AND MASS-ORIENTED CURRICULUM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10931, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"UNIVERSAL ACCESS TO QUALITY TERTIARY EDUCATION\"
rows.abstract:
Intends to establish a new higher education curriculum which shall: 

a) instill in every student the firm resolve never to allow our people to be dominated and controlled by foreign powers or domestic tyrants, developing a self-reliant and independent national economy with particular emphasis on agrarian reform, agriculture and national industries.

c) equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to serve the Filipino nation and encourage study programs that respond to community needs through immersion into larger society that exists beyond their classrooms.

rows.author: I083;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING CRITICAL MEDIA AND INFORMATION LITERACY IN THE PHILIPPINES AND PRESCRIBING ITS MANDATORY INCLUSION IN THE EDUCATION SYSTEM AND CURRICULUM IN THE PHILIPPINES, FOR SUCH OTHER PURPOSES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Defines important terms as follows:

Alternative Media refers to media contents that fall outside the mainstream or dominant contents. 
Its contents are progressive, critical, pro-people and free from business and corporate interests.

Critical Media Literacy is educational response that expands the notion of literacy to include 
different forms of mass communication, popular culture, and new technologies. It deepens the potential
of literacy education to critically analyze relationships between media and audiences, information, 
and power. Along with this mainstream analysis, alternative media production empowers students to 
create their own messages that can challenge media texts and narratives.


Seeks to create a critical media literacy curriculum not only of high school students but even primary/elementary students to help in cultivating a more informed and well-educated public to combat the surge of false information in the wake of technological advancements and in developing critical thinking skills at a very young age.

Provides that all programs to be implemented and curriculum to be developed shall duly promote and safeguard the fundamental freedom of speech and expression, and shall be guided by the principles of critical media literacy education summarized as: a) Media is a COMPETENT TOOL; b) Media is EVOLVING; c) Media is produce in DIFFERENT MODES; and d) Media DOES NOT EXIST IN A VACCUUM.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2019-02-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING UNIVERSAL PENSION TO ALL SENIOR CITIZENS AGED SIXTY-FIVE (65) YEARS AND ABOVE, AND FOR THIS PURPOSE INTRODUCING PARAGRAPH (I) IN SECTION 2 AND AMENDING SECTION 5 (H)(1) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES\", AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC  ACT NO. 9257, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZENS ACT OF 2003\", AND AS FURTHER AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9994, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZENS ACT OF 2010\"

senior citizens aged 65 years old and above and to INDIGENT senior citizens aged 60 - 64

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PENSION AND HEALTH BENEFITS TO COMFORT WOMEN, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines \"comfort women\" as Filipino women who were made sex slaves by the Japanese Occupation Army during World War II as may be determined by the National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women (NCRFW).

Proposes for a program for the proper counselling and guidance of \"comfort women\" and the provision of free full medical insurance through PhilHealth and a monthly pension of Three Thousand Pesos (Php3,000) to be provided by the Philippine Veterans Affairs Office (PVAO).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2019-02-07

rows.abstract:
Intends to enhance the benefits granted in Republic Act No.11164 which raised the monthly pension of war veterans.

Proposes a provision on the rules of succession for the beneficiaries of the pension wherein the spouse or the eldest legitimate child shall be allowed to receive the pension upon death of the war veteran.

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 83 OF THE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Intends to help ease the burden of employees in commuting to work by allowing alternative working arrangements.

Proposes to remove the limiting \"normal work hours\" from eight (8) hours a day for five (5) days to a more flexible work duration which means that employees may clock in to work at any time as long as they complete the required number of hours.

Proposes further to put a ceiling on the number of working hours to forty-eight (48) hours per week in order to protect the well-being of employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2019-02-07

rows.author: I116;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SHARED PARENTAL LEAVE POLICY THAT GRANTS AN OPTION TO FEMALE WORKERS IN THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE AND IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR TO SHARE THEIR LEAVE BENEFITS WITH THEIR SPOUSES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes that all covered female workers stated herein may, at her option, allocate up to sixty (60)
days of leave benefits to the child's father, whether or not the same is married to the female worker.

States that such shared period of leave shall be in addition to the seven (7) days paternity leave granted 
under R.A.8187 (Paternity Leave Act); shall be granted in every instance of pregnancy or miscarriage, 
regardless of frequency; and that in case of miscarriage, a period of only thirty (30) days can be allocated to the child's father.

Proposes further that in case of death, absence or incapacity of the male partner/spouse, the benefit
may be allocated to an alternative caregiver who may be a relative or the current partner of the female worker sharing the same household, upon election of the mother.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2019-05-20

rows.abstract:
Proposes to deter unscrupulous contractors from borrowing or lending a contractor's license
for a fee or commission by punishing such acts in order to prevent, if not totally eradicate, 
the said practice which is inimical to public safety and interest.

Amends Sec.35 of \"Contractors' License Law\" with an imprisonment of one to two years, 
or a fine of P200,000.00 to P1,000,000.00, or both, at the discretion of the court.
